data.title: Import & Export
data.tagline: Import and export move data in bulk: export saves records into files like CSV or Excel, import turns a file back into records.
data.learningOutcome: You know export hands you the data file itself and import loads a file back in; on garbled text you recognize the encoding problem and ask for a UTF-8 re-export.
data.description: Export 200 quotes as a CSV for the accountant, and import the edited file back—data moves between tools as files. Both operate on whole batches, not single records. If Excel shows garbled Chinese, it is usually an encoding problem; ask the AI to re-export as UTF-8.

learning.assumes: You have opened a spreadsheet file and downloaded attachments.
learning.outcome: You know export hands you the data file itself and import loads a file back in; on garbled text you recognize the encoding problem and ask for a UTF-8 re-export.

distinctions.label: CRUD
distinctions.explanation: CRUD operates on records one at a time; Import & Export moves the whole batch as files.

distinctions.label: API
distinctions.explanation: API moves data automatically between programs; Import & Export moves it manually via files.

explanation.title: Export: data becomes a file
explanation.text: The whole list is written into one CSV or Excel file that other software can open, edit, and archive.

explanation.title: Import: a file becomes records
explanation.text: Pick a file in the right format and each row becomes a record. Confirm the headers match your fields first.

explanation.title: It is an extra feature
explanation.text: CRUD works record by record; import and export move whole batches. Tell the AI whether this round includes them so the tool does not balloon.

data.boundary: Exporting is not sharing a link: a link is an entrance, a file is the data itself. Importing adds or overwrites records—back up first, or ask the AI for a "preview the rows to import" step. Garbled Chinese in Excel is usually encoding, fixed by asking for UTF-8 with BOM.

lessonPractice.title: An accountant needs all 200 customer records as a file she can edit in Excel. Which option actually gives her the data?

options.label: Send her the records as a CSV file
options.feedback: Correct. Exporting turns the whole batch into one file you can open in Excel or another tool.

options.label: Sending the web link to a colleague
options.feedback: Sharing a link only grants access; the data stays in the tool and no file changes hands.

options.label: Deleting 200 old records at once
options.feedback: Batch deletion is delete at scale—the data is gone, not moved.

data.agentPrompt: Add an "Export CSV" button to the quote list: export all fields, UTF-8 encoding so Excel shows Chinese correctly. Skip import until the next round.
